newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-West Australian says conditions mixed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-West Australian says conditions mixed.

text.p: West Australian Newspapers Holdings Ltd said on Thursday that its 6.6 percent fall in 1996/97 first half net profit to A$25.312 million reflected mixed trading conditions which improved after a difficult first quarter.

Trading conditions had not improved much since the end of the first half, the company said. The latest result included an abnormal loss of A$574,000 from employee redundancy and retraining costs and compared with the year-ago result when there was one additional week's trading.

The 4.1 percent fall in operating profit before tax and abnormal items to A$40.424 million was almost entirely due to the disparity in trading weeks, said the company, which publishes Perth's West Australian broadsheet newspaper.
Group operating revenue fell 1.2 percent to A$152.1 million.

"Trading conditions in the second quarter improved after a difficult first quarter, however, the real estate industry in Western Australia is still experiencing tough conditions and this has adversely affected the company's advertising revenue."
Net advertising revenue fell 2.6 percent to A$90.47 million and net circulation revenue fell 0.8 percent to A$27.8 million.

"While trading conditions have not materially improved since the end of the first half and the outlook is for only a gradual improvement in advertising volumes, some relief from high newsprint prices is expected in the second half," it said.

"In the first half the newsprint price per tonne was 5.5 percent higher than last year, however, the price for the second half is expected to be below the corresponding period last year," the company said.
West Australian shares were seven cents higher at A$5.25 at 3.05 p.m. (0405 GMT).
